summary: The talk addresses the gap between rapidly improving LLM reasoning capabilities and slowly improving search tools, which the speakers call the 'knowledge gap' or 'Oracle gap.' Using two benchmarks—BrowseComp Plus (OpenAI) and OfficeQA Pro (Databricks)—they demonstrate that Oracle performance is 93% and 64% respectively, but Codex with default tools only achieves 9 and 8 points. By providing Mixedbread's latent interaction search, most of the gap closes (BrowseComp within 3 points of Oracle, OfficeQA Pro nearly closed). The speakers explain that models write poor semantic queries—keyword-stuffed 'gibberish'—because they are trained primarily for coding tasks (using grep) and web tools optimized for human keyword patterns. Additionally, benchmarks like BEIR and NanoBEIR use 'Caveman style' entity queries that structurally favor BM25. To address this, they built a search agent with four tools: overview search (up to 50 chunk summaries), semantic search (top 10 full chunks), filter chunks (metadata facets), and grep (keyword match). The harness allows up to 4 search rounds with parallel searches, starting from an initial semantic search preview plus metadata hints for planning. Five principles encourage better queries: goal framing, distinct tool purposes, task framing that tricks the model into writing natural sentences instead of 'search queries,' prompt examples, and providing original query semantic results. Training uses a small LLM with supervised fine-tuning from a larger teacher, followed by on-policy reinforcement learning with a combined retrieval reward (NDCG + LLM rubric judging) and trajectory reward (query quality and exploration efficiency). Intermediate results show NDCG@10 of 0.4 on Oblique Congress versus 0.18 for GPT's multi-hop agent, and a production beta ranks top 1 on Snowflake's matchQA benchmark at 93.4% accuracy with Gemini 3.5 Flash, with less effort than comparable systems.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & The Knowledge Gap
sections.summary: Hanna and Amir introduce themselves from Mixedbread AI. They frame the core problem: LLM reasoning improves exponentially while search improves slowly, creating a 'knowledge gap' between reasoning capabilities and retrieval tools that serve as the main access pattern for knowledge in domains like legal and finance.

sections.title: Benchmark Evidence & Oracle Gap
sections.summary: They present BrowseComp Plus (OpenAI, 100k document corpus) and OfficeQA Pro (Databricks, US treasuries over 100 years). Oracle performance is 93% and 64% respectively, but Codex with default tools drops to 9 and 8 points. Mixedbread's latent interaction search recovers most of the gap, demonstrating that retrieval—not reasoning—is the bottleneck.

sections.title: Why Models Write Poor Queries
sections.summary: Models write keyword-stuffed 'gibberish' queries because they are trained for coding tasks (grep/regex), trained to use web tools optimized for human keyword patterns, and biased by benchmarks like BEIR/NanoBEIR that use 'Caveman style' entity queries favoring BM25. The agent guesses keywords to maximize overlap rather than using powerful semantic search.

sections.title: Search Agent Harness Design
sections.summary: Their agent has four tools: overview search (up to 50 chunk summaries), semantic search (top 10 full chunks), filter chunks (metadata facets), and grep (keyword match). The harness allows up to 4 search rounds with parallel searches per round. The agent starts with the user query plus initial semantic search results and metadata hints, splits search intent into up to 4 queries, picks the best tool for each, deduplicates results, and submits a final ranking.

sections.title: Principles for Better Query Writing
sections.summary: Five principles encourage better queries: goal framing (articulate needed evidence before querying), distinct tools (semantic for aspects, grep for exact keywords), task framing (instruct model to write a concise sentence describing what it wants, not a 'search query'), prompt examples showing good queries and aspect splitting, and providing original query semantic search results for corpus language awareness.

sections.title: Training the Agent
sections.summary: They train a small LLM for speed. First supervised fine-tuning with a larger teacher, then on-policy reinforcement learning with a search reward combining a retrieval reward (NDCG + LLM rubric judging on relevance, chunk relevance, and ranking plausibility) and a trajectory reward (LLM judge evaluating query naturalness and exploration sufficiency). An example trajectory shows semantic queries as natural sentences and grep as keyword patterns.

sections.title: Results & Conclusion
sections.summary: Intermediate results: Oblique Congress NDCG@10 of 0.4 vs 0.18 for GPT multi-hop agent. Production beta (Mixedbread agentic search) ranks top 1 on Snowflake matchQA at 93.4% accuracy with Gemini 3.5 Flash, achieved with less effort than comparable LLMs. They conclude there is significant room for improvement in LLM search tools and invite applications.

organization.name: Mixedbread
organization.summary: Mixedbread is an independent retrieval company. Its first-party homepage and documentation present Mixedbread Search as a multimodal retrieval API (text, PDFs, images, video, 100+ languages) and Agentic Search as a hosted multi-round retrieval loop driven by Toast 1. Hanna Lichtenberg, the speaker, is an AI engineer leading agentic search at Mixedbread.
